finding.claim: Unauthenticated requests with unknown kid values force a synchronous JWKS refetch per request (no rate limit or negative cache), enabling IdP-side DoS amplification. Availability impact only; no signature bypass.
finding.source: kid header of an unverified token (jwt/jwks_client.py:239-241)

trace.note: cache skipped when refresh is set

finding.guards_checked: kid is exact string match (jwks_client.py:257); URI restricted to http/https (jwks_client.py:90-95); redirects disabled (jwks_client.py:17-27). No rate limit or negative caching present.

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, the lru_cache on get_signing_key never re-checks the current JWKS on hit, so a key removed from the JWKS (e.g. after compromise) keeps verifying tokens until LRU eviction (max 16) or process restart. Opt-in; default is cache_keys=False.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token signed by a key that the IdP has since removed from the JWKS
finding.sink: Signature verification accepting token using the cached PyJWK (jwt/api_jws.py:432)

trace.note: instance method replaced with cached wrapper
cache hit returns stale PyJWK without refresh
JWKS lifespan does not apply to per-key cache

finding.guards_checked: Default cache_keys=False (jwt/jwks_client.py:34). lifespan applies only to JWKS-level cache (jwt/jwk_set_cache.py:25-31).

finding.claim: Default enforce_minimum_key_length=False means HMAC secrets shorter than the digest size are accepted with only a warning, enabling offline brute force of a weak secret given one valid token.
finding.source: Attacker possesses one valid HS256/384/512 token signed with a short application secret
finding.sink: HMAC verification with a weak key (jwt/algorithms.py:422-423)

trace.note: returns warning when key shorter than digest size
only raises if enforce flag set; otherwise warns

finding.guards_checked: Warning is emitted (api_jws.py:430); enforcement is available via option enforce_minimum_key_length (api_jws.py:427). Application-configuration risk rather than library bypass.
